description: Each type's count is the number of different transactions with behaviour analysis tied to its traders.

a.request: Link each advanced behaviour record to its transaction (`translink` = `transreg`) and then to that transaction's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`). Use exact text matches and drop anything without a match. For each trader type (`tradekind`), with a missing type as its own group, count the distinct transactions (`transreg`) that have behaviour records. Count each transaction once, even when two behaviour records point to it. Compute each type's share as its count divided by the total of the counts across all types. Which trader types have a share strictly above the plain average of the per-type shares? For each one, show the type, its count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
a.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), s AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM t) AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT s.tradekind, s.cnt AS count, s.share AS share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE a.avg_share IS NOT NULL AND s.share > a.avg_share

b.request: Count, for each trader type (`tradekind`, with a missing type as its own group), the distinct transactions that have an advanced behaviour analysis linked through `translink` = `transreg` and on to the trader through `trdref` = `tradereg` using exact matches (unmatched rows dropped). Compute each type's share as its count divided by the sum of counts across all types, then return the types whose share is strictly above the unrounded plain average of the per-type shares (nothing if that average is missing), showing type, count, share, and share minus average
b.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), s AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT tradekind, cnt AS count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM a WHERE avg_share IS NOT NULL AND share > avg_share

c.request: Taking the advanced behaviour analyses linked to their transaction (`translink` = `transreg`) and on to that transaction's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`), using exact text matches and dropping anything that doesn't match: how much behaviour analysis does each trader type (`tradekind`) have? Treat a missing type as its own group. Compute each type's share as its count divided by the total of the counts across all types. Which trader types have a share strictly above the plain average of the per-type shares? For each one, show the type, its count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing. Each type's count is the number of different transactions with behaviour analysis tied to its traders.
c.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT a.translink) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord r ON a.translink = r.transreg JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), s AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), g AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT tradekind, cnt AS count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM g WHERE avg_share IS NOT NULL AND share > avg_share

d.request: Taking the advanced behaviour analyses linked to their transaction (`translink` = `transreg`) and on to that transaction's trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`), using exact text matches and dropping anything that doesn't match: for each trader type (`tradekind`), with a missing type treated as its own group, count the number of different transactions that have behaviour analysis tied to that type's traders. Compute each type's share as its count divided by the total of the counts across all types. Which trader types have a share strictly above the plain average of the per-type shares? For each one, show the type, its count, its share, and its share minus the average share. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
d.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON ab.translink = tr.transreg JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), shares AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, CAST(cnt AS REAL) / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM counts) AS share FROM counts), avgs AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT s.tradekind, s.cnt AS count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avgs a WHERE a.avg_share IS NOT NULL AND s.share > a.avg_share
